item.title: Village courts set for major change as Bougainville prepares new system
item.description: A new training for magistrates, clerks and peace officers is underway in Arawa as Bougainville prepares to bring its Community Court system into operation. The training is being held by the Community Court and Land Mediation Directorate under the Department of Justice and Legal Services, ahead of the Bougainville Community Court Act 2024 coming into force.
item.content:encoded:
A new training for magistrates, clerks and peace officers is underway in Arawa as Bougainville prepares to bring its Community Court system into operation.

The training is being held by the Community Court and Land Mediation Directorate under the Department of Justice and Legal Services, ahead of the Bougainville Community Court Act 2024 coming into force.

For officials who have worked under the Village Court system, the training is an important step as they prepare for their new roles under the Community Court.

Bougainville now has the Bougainville Court and the Bougainville Community Court, after the system was passed by the House of Representatives in 2024.

This gives Bougainville its own court system, separate from Papua New Guinea.

Over the past few years, officials from Bougainville, the PNG Department of Justice and Attorney General, the Australia-Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Partnership Program [APLJ], and the PNG Department of Justice and Attorney General have been working on the transfer of functions and personnel from the Village Courts to the new Community Courts.

The first region-wide training is now taking place in Arawa for officials from Central Bougainville.

It was opened by Secretary for the Department of Justice and Legal Services, Leontine Ivano, alongside Central Bougainville Law and Justice Sector Coordinator Dennis Kuiai and Central District Coordinator Tonny Moera.

Micah Forukave from the Directorate of Community Court and Land Mediation says the training is important before the new law comes into operation.

He says officials need to understand their new roles and responsibilities, including their powers and limits, which will be different from the Village Court system.

APLJ Advisor Benjamin Bofeng is facilitating the training with staff from the Directorate of Community Court and Land Mediation.

The Bougainville Community Court Act is expected to come into operation in September once it is formally gazetted and endorsed.

There are currently 46 Village Courts across Bougainville, which will become Community Courts once the new law comes into operation.

The number of Community Courts is also expected to increase to make the local courts more accessible to people across Bougainville.

item.title: Police minister challenges officers to raise standards
item.description: Police Minister Sir John Pundari has thanked long-serving members of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary and challenged serving officers to uphold the police oath and raise professional standards. Sir John made the remarks during his recent visit to Lae, where he was welcomed with a police parade at the Lae Central Police Station.
item.content:encoded:
Police Minister Sir John Pundari has thanked long-serving members of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary and challenged serving officers to uphold the police oath and raise professional standards.

Sir John made the remarks during his recent visit to Lae, where he was welcomed with a police parade at the Lae Central Police Station.

The Minister used the occasion to recognize officers who have dedicated decades of service to the country.

He described policing as a high-risk responsibility, saying many officers have lost their lives while protecting their communities.

“As a son of a policeman myself, from the bottom of my heart, I want to say thank you for your services to your people and to the country you love,” Pundari said.

Sir John also recognised Assistant Commissioner of Police for Northern Command, Peter Guinness, who is preparing to retire after more than 50 years of service.

He said Guinness's long career represents the dedication of many police officers who have served in different parts of Papua New Guinea.

The minister urged serving officers to remain faithful to the oath they took when joining the force.

“Standards start with you. Be the face of the law. Be the love of this nation,” he said.

He said discipline must begin at home and continue into the workplace.

Police officers, he said, must protect the people, uphold the law and maintain public trust.

Pundari also warned that officers who breach their oath will face disciplinary action.

He said the police force must use the next 50 years to improve its standards and service to the people.

“This is the time to change. This is the time to be better as we reset for the next 50 years,” he said.

Pundari said the future of policing must focus on higher standards, discipline, accountability and better service to communities.

He called on officers to remain committed to protecting the people and serving the country they have sworn to protect.

item.title: 22 foreign nationals caught in Bougainville mining crackdown
item.description: 22 foreign nationals have been taken to Buka for further processing following an enforcement operation targeting unauthorised mining activities in Kopani, Asikopan-Torau Constituency, Central Bougainville. The Autonomous Bougainville Government, in a statement released on Sunday, said the operation was carried out in the early hours of Sunday 23 August 2026 by the Bougainville Police Service and t
item.content:encoded:
22 foreign nationals have been taken to Buka for further processing following an enforcement operation targeting unauthorised mining activities in Kopani, Asikopan-Torau Constituency, Central Bougainville.

The Autonomous Bougainville Government, in a statement released on Sunday, said the operation was carried out in the early hours of Sunday 23 August 2026 by the Bougainville Police Service and the Department of Mining and Petroleum, in collaboration with relevant enforcement agencies.

The 22 foreign nationals were removed from Kopani and transported to Buka for further processing by the relevant authorities.

Enforcement officers also seized and impounded machinery, which included excavators, a backhoe, large trucks, a mining wash pant, a land cruiser and other mining machinery and equipment.

The ABG says the equipment is being secured pending completion of the legal processes.

President and Minister for Mining and Petroleum, Ishmael Toroama, says the Government has spent the past three years conducting awareness on unauthorised mining and the requirements of Bougainville's mining laws.

“For the past three years, the ABG has undertaken extensive awareness with landowners, miners, communities and other stakeholders across Bougainville on unauthorised mining activities and the requirements of our mining laws.

''By now, our people and stakeholders should know and understand the law. The period of awareness has been sufficient; it is now time for enforcement of Bougainville's laws.”

President Toroama says enforcement will apply equally to foreign nationals and Bougainvilleans involved in unlawful mining activities.

“Our laws exist to protect the interests of Bougainville and its people. No individual, company or foreign national is above the law.

''The Government will continue its investigations, and appropriate legal action will also be taken against local individuals found to have facilitated, supported, or participated in unauthorised mining activities.

''If you wish to participate in Bougainville's mining sector, you must do so legally and in accordance with the laws of Bougainville” President Toroama said.

The ABG says equipment seized during the operation could be forfeited under the mining laws. Anyone claiming ownership of the equipment can apply to the court within 30 days to have it returned.

The Government has thanked police, immigration and Department of Mining and Petroleum officers, as well as those who provided logistical support during the operation.

The ABG says it will continue to conduct enforcement operations as needed to protect Bougainville's mineral resources and ensure mining activities are carried out legally and responsibly.

item.title: Bougainville placed on drought alert
item.description: Bougainville has been placed on drought alert, with the Autonomous Bougainville Government warning of possible water and food shortages due to the prolonged dry conditions. In a statement released on Sunday, the ABG Department of Community Government, District Affairs and Emergency Disaster Services says the alert follows a warning from the PNG National Weather Service about below-normal rainfall
item.content:encoded:
Bougainville has been placed on drought alert, with the Autonomous Bougainville Government warning of possible water and food shortages due to the prolonged dry conditions.

In a statement released on Sunday, the ABG Department of Community Government, District Affairs and Emergency Disaster Services says the alert follows a warning from the PNG National Weather Service about below-normal rainfall linked to the current El Niño weather pattern.

The ABG says there is an 80 to 90 percent chance of below-normal rainfall across Bougainville between September and November 2026.

It says the El Niño conditions are also expected to continue through the rest of the year.

The ABG is concerned about water supplies, food gardens, and food security, especially in remote and outer-island communities.

The Nissan Atolls and other outer-island communities in Northern Bougainville will receive priority monitoring because of their vulnerability and limited access to alternative water sources, transport and essential services.

The ABG says prolonged dry conditions could lead to:

Other parts of Bougainville, including Central and South Bougainville, may experience different weather conditions, but the drought risk is being monitored across the entire region.

Disaster officials will conduct rapid assessments in vulnerable communities over the next two to four weeks and will increase weekly drought monitoring and reporting.

The ABG is also working to finalise a drought contingency plan to guide preparedness and early response.

Communities have been urged to conserve water, protect available water sources, monitor their food gardens and report water shortages to their local community governments and district authorities.

The public has also been advised to follow official updates from the PNG National Weather Service and the ABG and avoid unverified information.

The ABG says Bougainville will remain on HIGH WATCH for drought and water-security risks through 2026, with RED priority monitoring for vulnerable outer-island communities.

However, it says the alert does not mean all communities are currently experiencing severe drought.

item.title: One dead in a hit and run in Madang
item.description: A motorist was arrested in Madang today following an early morning hit- and- run incident along the Modilon Road. The victim, in his late 20s and from a mixed parentage of Madang and East Sepik, died instantly.
item.content:encoded:
A motorist was arrested in Madang today following an early morning hit- and- run incident along the Modilon Road.

The victim, in his late 20s and from a mixed parentage of Madang and East Sepik, died instantly.

The deceased, believed to be an employee of PNG Pawa, was walking alone along the Modilon Road between 3 and 4am today when he was hit by a speeding vehicle.

The incident was captured by CCTV cameras at nearby shops, with police using the footage to identify the vehicle involved.

Police tracked down a black taxi and apprehended its driver. They have yet to release an official statement on the incident, but an investigation is now underway.

The vehicle remains in police custody as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident.

Today's incident is the second fatal accident along the Modilon Road in just over a week.

The first case occurred at the Holy Spirit school crossing, in which an elderly pedestrian was knocked over by a vehicle, resulting in instant death also.

item.title: PNGFA assured of players’ outstanding allowances
item.description: The PNG Football Association has confirmed its participation in this year’s Melanesian Spearhead Group Prime Minister’s Cup, following an assurance from the Office of the Prime Minister that unresolved payments from previous tournaments will be settled. Last week, PNGFA released a statement indicating it was considering pulling out of the tournament. General Secretary Armjad Tekwie said the statem
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Football Association has confirmed its participation in this year’s Melanesian Spearhead Group Prime Minister’s Cup, following an assurance from the Office of the Prime Minister that unresolved payments from previous tournaments will be settled.

Last week, PNGFA released a statement indicating it was considering pulling out of the tournament. General Secretary Armjad Tekwie said the statement was made in fairness to the players and their concerns.

“PNGFA did release a statement indicating that we were considering pulling out of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup if certain commitments were not met,” Tekwie said.

“Since releasing the statement, we have had successful meetings with the Office of the Prime Minister. We have been assured that all requirements for the players will be met.”

Following the positive feedback from the Office of the Prime Minister, PNGFA is now assembling both the men’s and women’s teams for the fifth edition of the tournament.

“We have been advised to assemble both teams and commence preparations,” Tekwie added.

“I just want to clarify that our concerns were based on outstanding allowances for players from 2024 and 2025. We have provided all necessary documentation and have been assured that this is a priority and will be addressed. We are scheduled to depart on September 14,” he said.

“There were questions coming from all angles, so we felt compelled to declare our position.

“Of course we wanted to ensure that we participate in the MSG, but we also felt that we owed it to the players to ensure that, in fairness, whatever outstanding commitments made to them in good faith are satisfied before we commit to participating.”

As of Thursday, August 20, this newsroom was told that payments totaling around K469,000 are yet to be made.

“We were assured that payments will be made before the teams leave for Fiji, and so we are still waiting,” Tekwie said.

Tekwie recalled that since December 2025, they had been advised to liaise directly with the Host Organising Committee. However, after all attempts failed, they went directly to the Office of the Prime Minister.

“We managed to reach out to the Office of the Prime Minister and we successfully did so after the publication of the press statement,” he said.

With the long delay, PNG Football advocate and initiator of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup, Joseph Ealedona, has called for an audit and investigation into the issue, which he described as unfair to the players.

“Whatever is happening to the players is unfair and something needs to be done, and some people need to be held responsible,” Ealedona said.

As this newsroom continues to follow the issue, the men’s draw for the tournament has been released, with the women’s draw yet to be announced.

item.title: Simbu farmers appeal for continued support as MVF project nears completion
item.description: Local farmers in Simbu Province are calling on stakeholders to establish follow-up assistance programs as the Market for Village Farmers (MVF) project prepares to end operations this September. Funded to help smallholder farmers shift from subsistence farming to market-driven agribusiness, the MVF initiative has impacted an estimated 25,000 farming households, or around 125,000 people across six p
item.content:encoded:
Local farmers in Simbu Province are calling on stakeholders to establish follow-up assistance programs as the Market for Village Farmers (MVF) project prepares to end operations this September.

Funded to help smallholder farmers shift from subsistence farming to market-driven agribusiness, the MVF initiative has impacted an estimated 25,000 farming households, or around 125,000 people across six provinces.

In Simbu, the project has delivered significant economic growth. But farmers say without continued institutional support, the progress made could be lost.

Operating under a Public-Private-Producer Partnership model, MVF provided capacity building, infrastructure support and financial grants that allowed rural families to reinvest in their homes and local economies.

A potato farmer from Yuai in Kundiawa-Gembogl District and father of two, Willie Peter, said the project was a turning point.

"Through the assistance from the MVF project, I managed to build a permanent home for my family costing K18,000, while also comfortably covering my children’s school fees," Peter said.

Fellow farmer Jacinta Essy used the support to diversify into business.

"The MVF initiative gave me the financial leverage to build and open my own trade store valued at K20,000, securing a steady secondary income for my household, "Essy said.

According to Provincial Coordinator for MVF in Simbu and Officer-in-Charge at the Fresh Produce Development Agency (FPDA), David Kaupa, led the country in implementation with 10 lead partners and over 3,800 lead farmers.

- K3 million+ disbursed to more than 1,333 households across eight active partnerships

- 1,326 tonnes increase in local produce output, generating K2.3 million in direct revenue

- Contact Farmer Grants of K4,080 for agro-inputs under a 70/30 co-funding model

- Lead Farmer Grants of K10,000+ for high-tech tools including solar irrigation and walk-behind tractors

- Transport support to four lead commercial partners

- Financial literacy, crop production and nutrition training for over 3,000 households

- Major feeder road upgrades including Las Wara Road in Sinesine-Yongomugl and Awagle–Dindim Road in Kerowagi, set to connect over 4,000 households across four wards to markets

Mr. Kaupa said the program successfully equipped farmers with self-sustaining skills. However, community leaders say the demand for structured support remains high.

With the September closure approaching, Simbu farmers are urging government and development partners to replicate the 4P model in future rural development programs to ensure the next generation of smallholders can achieve similar financial independence.

item.title: Bekut prison fencing underway in Buka Island
item.description: Work is finally underway for a new high-security fencing to securely confine prisoners and remandees at Bekut Prison on Buka Island. The project for proper fencing is funded by Australia's Department of Forrign Affairs and Trdae through the Australia-Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Program, APLJ.
item.content:encoded:
Work is finally underway for a new high-security fencing to securely confine prisoners and remandees at Bekut Prison on Buka Island.

The project for proper fencing is funded by Australia's Department of Forrign Affairs and Trdae through the Australia-Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Program, APLJ.

It was launched early this year with a groundbreaking ceremony, however work is only starting after the initial contractor was swapped.

Bougainville Joint Venture is now taking carriage of the K6.6 million contract, which will see new and proper high-security prison fencing around the male confinement area, together with new buildings (and fencing) for female and juveniles and associated works.

Future development works are expected to include a new guard house, expanded accommodation, solar power, and upgraded ablution facilities.

Chief of Bougainville Correctional Service Assistant Commissioner, Vincent Kundi visited the work at the prison this week, pleased that work has finally taken off and confident of the contractor meeting duration of the work.

He dscribed the development as a critical step for Bougainville’s justice sector saying it will improve detainee management, staff welfare, and facility operations, thanking the Australian Government through the APLJ program and alao acknowledging the support from the Autonomous Bougainville Government Department of Justice and Legal Services and sector agencies.

Confinement at Bekut Prison has been a major public concern in Bougainville for many years.

The lack of secure detainment has seen prisoners and remandees walking off at will, challenging the authority of the courts and questioning the capability of the correctional service.

Assistant Commissioner Kundi says the days of prisoners and detainees taking Bekut Prison as a holiday camp is almost up, assuring the public that a safer, confined prison will soon be in place.

He says all project stakeholders will see the work through to its conclusion, which will reinforce the law and justice sector in Bougainville, improving safety for officers and detainees and lift standards at Bekut.
